sentences.text: At a rally in Montana this October, President Trump told the crowd that "tariffs don't cause inflation".

assertions.text: Trump said at his Kalispell, Montana rally that tariffs don't cause inflation.

sentences.note: Source title: 'President Trump Delivers Emphatic Remarks at Kalispell, Montana Rally - 10/14/26'.

sentences.text: If he is right, a tariff costs shoppers nothing extra. If he is wrong, somebody here is paying it.
In his State of the Union, Trump said who he thinks pays: countries that were ripping us off "are now paying us hundreds of billions of dollars".

assertions.text: In the State of the Union, Trump said countries are now paying the US hundreds of billions of dollars.

quote.text: are now paying us hundreds of billions of dollars
quote.speaker: Trump

sentences.note: Source title: 'WATCH: Trump says tariffs could replace income tax | 2026 State of the Union' (PBS NewsHour).

sentences.text: On his channel, Patrick Boyle puts it the other way round: "A tariff is just a tax paid by Americans, not by Canadians."

assertions.text: Patrick Boyle said a tariff is just a tax paid by Americans, not by Canadians.

quote.text: A tariff is just a tax paid by Americans, not by Canadians.
quote.speaker: Patrick Boyle

sentences.note: Channel: Patrick Boyle. The context is his video on Canadian auto-parts tariffs.

sentences.text: They cannot both be right. So follow the cost, starting at the border.
If foreign sellers were paying, they would have cut their prices to make room for the tariff, so economists at the New York Fed checked their prices with the tariff taken out.

assertions.text: The NY Fed regressions take as the dependent variable import prices exclusive of tariffs, that is, foreign export prices, to estimate how much of the tariff incidence foreign exporters bore.

sentences.text: In the first eight months of 2025, a 10 percent tariff cut those prices by only 0.6 percentage points, which by the Fed's estimate left 94 percent of the cost with American importers.

assertions.text: In the first eight months of 2025, a 10 percent tariff caused only a 0.6 percentage point decline in foreign export prices.
qualifications: The sentence says 'by the Fed's estimate': these are regression estimates on import unit values.

assertions.text: 94 percent of the tariff incidence was borne by U.S. importers in January-August 2025.

sentences.text: Foreign sellers did start giving more ground late in the year, yet in November importers still carried 86 percent.

assertions.text: A larger share of the tariff incidence was borne by foreign exporters by the end of 2025; in November the incidence on U.S. importers was 86 percent.

sentences.text: But an importer paying at the border is not yet a shopper paying at the till. How much of it reaches the shelf?

A New York Fed staff report on the 2025 tariffs estimates that consumer prices rise by about 26 percent of the tariff increase, roughly a quarter of the tariff rate, measured against goods less exposed to the tariffs.

assertions.text: Studying the 2025 U.S. tariffs, the staff report finds about 26 percent of the tariff increase passes through to consumer prices, measured relative to less-exposed goods with aggregate conditions held fixed.
qualifications: The sentence says it is measured against less-exposed goods; s21 adds what that leaves out.

sentences.text: And not all of that comes from imports: 36 percent of it comes from goods made at home, because American producers pay more for imported parts, and with foreign rivals pricier, they raise their markups.

assertions.text: 36 percent of the consumer price increase arises indirectly: tariffs raise the cost of imported inputs used by U.S. producers, and domestic producers raise their markups because they face less competition from higher-priced imports.

sentences.text: Nor does it arrive the day a tariff is announced.

In the New York Fed's estimates, about half of the direct effect on imported goods is in shop prices after three months, and all of it after six, as retailers take a few months to pass on higher costs.

assertions.text: The direct effect of higher import prices: about half is in place after 3 months and all of it by 6 months, as retailers take a few months to pass on higher costs.

sentences.text: The part that runs through American-made goods is slower still, taking nine to twelve months to work through supply chains.

assertions.text: The indirect effect takes 9 to 12 months to work its way through supply chains.

sentences.text: Firms in the New York Fed's business surveys gave their reasons for spreading increases out: some sell under fixed-price contracts they cannot change until they expire, and some raise prices a little at a time to avoid shocking customers.

assertions.text: In NY Fed business surveys, some businesses cited fixed-price contracts they cannot raise until expiry, and some a 'trickle up' approach of gradual increases to avoid shocking customers.

sentences.text: So is a tariff a one-time bump in prices, or lasting inflation?

The New York Fed estimates the tariffs' effect on the level of consumer goods prices peaked near 3 percent in February 2026, and forecasts it to ease to about 2 percent by August after a Supreme Court ruling cut some tariffs, then edge up again with new tariffs on Canadian goods.

assertions.text: The tariff effect on the consumer goods price level peaked near 3 percent in February 2026; the forecast has it easing to about 2 percent by August 2026, reflecting the early-2026 tariff cut after a U.S. Supreme Court ruling, and edging up again after August 2026 mainly because of the tariffs on Canadian goods.
qualifications: s19 carries the survey limitation that 'one-time' is drawn out in practice.

sentences.text: Its contribution to the yearly rise in consumer goods prices also peaked that February, at 2.9 percentage points, and is forecast to fall to around zero by August.

assertions.text: The tariff contribution to twelve-month changes in consumer goods prices peaked in February 2026 at 2.9 percentage points and is forecast to fall to around zero by August 2026.
qualifications: s19 carries the survey limitation that 'one-time' is drawn out in practice.

sentences.text: But the Fed's survey researchers warn that "one-time" can be "a drawn-out affair, especially when the tariffs change frequently", with many firms spreading price increases across extended periods.

assertions.text: NY Fed survey researchers write that a one-time price-level adjustment may in practice be a drawn-out affair, especially when the tariffs change frequently, with many firms spreading price increases across extended periods.

quote.text: a drawn-out affair, especially when the tariffs change frequently

qualifications: This is the qualification itself: the one-time adjustment is drawn out in practice.

sentences.text: So who pays? By the Fed's estimates, mostly not foreign sellers: American importers carried the bulk of the 2025 tariffs, and part of that cost reached consumer prices, including for goods made at home.

assertions.text: U.S. firms and consumers bore the bulk of the economic burden of the 2025 tariffs; foreign exporters bore a small share.
The 2025 tariffs had economically and statistically significant effects on consumer prices, including through goods made at home.

sentences.text: What these estimates cannot give you is the economy-wide inflation rate: they compare goods more and less exposed to tariffs, and leave out effects through the exchange rate and the Fed's monetary-policy response.

assertions.text: Because the results rest on differences in tariff exposure across goods, they capture relative price effects rather than the economy-wide component of inflation, and do not account for the tariff impact on the exchange rate or the monetary-policy response.

sentences.text: Within those limits, the tariffs look more like a step up in prices than lasting inflation, though a step that firms are taking slowly.

assertions.text: Tariffs have left consumer goods price levels higher while their effect on inflation fades; in practice many firms spread the increases across extended periods.
qualifications: The sentence carries the survey limitation: firms are taking the step slowly.

sentences.text: Next time someone says another country pays a tariff, ask one question: did that country's sellers cut their prices?
And when a tariff changes, don't judge it by next week's receipts; the goods made at home take the better part of a year to catch up.

assertions.text: The indirect effect through domestically produced goods takes 9 to 12 months to work its way through supply chains.

sentences.note: Points back in words to s14's nine to twelve months; no new figure.
